relevance_reason: Population-scale study of PRKN mutation frequency, with CNV characterization and risk of PD for heterozygous carriers; relevant to inheritance and population genetics of PARK2.

findings.statement: Zhu et al. (2022) evaluated PRKN mutations, including SNVs and copy number variants, in the UK Biobank (whole exome sequencing and genotyping array data from 200,606 participants) and found a pathogenic PRKN mutation in 1.8% of participants and 2 mutations in approximately 1 in 7,800 participants.
quotes: In the UK Biobank, we found a pathogenic PRKN mutation in 1.8% of participants and two mutations in ∼1/7800 participants.

findings.statement: Zhu et al. (2022) found that UK Biobank participants carrying 1 pathogenic PRKN variant were as likely as noncarriers to have Parkinson disease (OR 0.91, 0.58-1.38; P = 0.76) or a parent with Parkinson disease (OR 1.12; P = 0.19); similarly, in the NIH-PD + AMP-PD case-control cohort (whole genome sequencing of 4,094 participants), heterozygous carriers were not at increased risk (OR 1.29, 0.74-2.38; P = 0.43). The authors concluded that heterozygous pathogenic PRKN mutations are common but do not increase the risk of Parkinson disease.
quotes: Those with one PRKN pathogenic variant were as likely as non-carriers to have Parkinson's disease [odds ratio = 0.91 (0.58-1.38), P-value 0.76] or a parent with Parkinson's disease [odds ratio = 1.12 (0.94-1.31), P-value = 0.19].
Similarly, those in the NIH-PD + AMP + PD cohort with one PRKN pathogenic variant were as likely as non-carriers to have Parkinson's disease [odds ratio = 1.29 (0.74-2.38), P-value = 0.43].
Together our results demonstrate that heterozygous pathogenic PRKN mutations are common in the population but do not increase the risk of Parkinson's disease.

findings.statement: Zhu et al. (2022) identified 2,692 PRKN copy number variants from genotyping array data in the UK Biobank; deletions or duplications involving exon 2 accounted for roughly half of all CNVs, and 88% involved exons 2, 3, or 4. Using NIH-PD participants genotyped by whole genome sequencing, array, and MLPA, they validated genotyping arrays for CNV detection.
quotes: In the UK Biobank, we identified 2692 PRKN copy number variants from genotyping array data from nearly half a million participants (the largest collection to date).
Deletions or duplications involving exon 2 accounted for roughly half of all copy number variants and the vast majority (88%) involved exons 2, 3, or 4.
we validated genotyping array for the detection of copy number variants

findings.statement: In the NIH-PD cohort, Zhu et al. (2022) used functional assays of patient fibroblasts to resolve variants of unclear significance in biallelic PRKN carriers, and the results suggested that cryptic loss-of-function variants in monoallelic carriers are not a substantial confounder for association studies.
quotes: functional assays of patient fibroblasts resolved variants of unclear significance in biallelic carriers and suggested that cryptic loss of function variants in monoallelic carriers are not a substantial confounder for association studies

relevance_reason: Reports olfactory function in patients with early-onset PD who carry two Parkin mutations (compound heterozygotes) versus heterozygotes and noncarriers. This adds to the clinical description of PARK2.

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2011) gave the University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT) to 44 probands from the CORE-PD study whose Parkinson disease began at or before age 50 years. Of these, 9 were Parkin compound heterozygotes, 10 were heterozygotes and 25 were noncarriers. Compound heterozygotes had higher UPSIT scores (31.9) than heterozygotes (20.1) or noncarriers (19.9) (p less than 0.001), and this difference persisted after adjustment for age, gender, disease duration and smoking. The authors concluded that compound heterozygotes with PD have olfaction within the normal range.
quotes: Among probands with PD, compound heterozygotes had higher UPSIT scores (31.9) than heterozygotes (20.1) or noncarriers (19.9) (p < 0.001). These differences persisted after adjustment for age, gender, disease duration, and smoking.
Compound heterozygotes with PD have olfaction within the normal range.

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2011) found that olfaction was significantly reduced in PD patients who were heterozygous for a single Parkin mutation but not in their heterozygous relatives without PD. Among relatives without PD, UPSIT scores were similar in heterozygotes (32.5) and noncarriers (32.4), and better than in heterozygotes with PD (p = 0.001). The authors stated that further research is required to assess whether these findings reflect different neuropathology in Parkin mutation heterozygotes and compound heterozygotes.
quotes: Among relatives without PD, UPSIT performance was similar in heterozygotes (32.5) vs noncarriers (32.4), and better than in heterozygotes with PD (p = 0.001).
Olfaction is significantly reduced among Parkin mutation heterozygotes with PD but not among their heterozygous relatives without PD.
Further research is required to assess whether these findings reflect different neuropathology in Parkin mutation heterozygotes and compound heterozygotes.

phenotypes.text: reduced olfaction in Parkin heterozygotes with PD

relevance_reason: Large case-control study of PARK2 copy number variants in PD patients and controls. It reports patients with two mutations (homozygous or compound heterozygous) and finds no association between carrying one heterozygous mutation and PD.

findings.statement: Kay et al. (2010) screened 2,091 patients with Parkinson disease (mean onset age 58.3 years) and 1,686 controls for PARK2 deletions, multiplications, and copy number variations (CNVs), using semiquantitative PCR and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification, with validation by real-time quantitative PCR. The subjects had already been tested for point mutations. Thirteen patients had 2 CNV mutations, 5 had 1 CNV plus 1 point mutation, and 18 had 1 CNV mutation. The mutations found in patients spanned exons 2-9.
quotes: We studied 1,686 control subjects (mean age 66.1 ± 13.1 years) and 2,091 patients with PD (mean onset age 58.3 ± 12.1 years).
Thirteen patients had 2 CNV mutations, 5 had 1 CNV and 1 point mutation, and 18 had 1 CNV mutation. Mutations found in patients spanned exons 2-9.

findings.statement: Kay et al. (2010) found heterozygous PARK2 CNV mutations in 0.95% of 1,686 controls and 0.86% of 2,091 patients with Parkinson disease. All of the CNV mutations in the 16 carrier controls were in exons 1-4, which spare the exons encoding functionally critical protein domains.
quotes: A total of 0.95% of control subjects and 0.86% of patients carried a heterozygous CNV mutation.
CNV mutations found in 16 control subjects were all in exons 1-4, sparing exons that encode functionally critical protein domains.

findings.statement: In white subjects, Kay et al. (2010) found that carrying 1 PARK2 CNV did not increase the risk of Parkinson disease (odds ratio 1.05, p = 0.89) and was not associated with earlier onset (64.7 years in heterozygotes vs 58.5 years in noncarriers). They concluded that there was no compelling evidence that heterozygous PARK2 mutations, alone or combined with known risk factors (SNCA, MAPT, APOE, smoking, coffee intake), are associated with PD.
quotes: In whites, having 1 CNV was not associated with increased risk (odds ratio 1.05, p = 0.89) or earlier onset of PD (64.7 ± 8.6 heterozygous vs 58.5 ± 11.8 normal).
There is no compelling evidence for association of heterozygous PARK2 mutations, by themselves or in combination with known risk factors, with PD.

relevance_reason: A multicenter cohort study of early-onset PD that reports how often PRKN mutations occur, how often they occur in Hispanic patients, and how they relate to age at onset. It adds supporting population and phenotype data for PARK2; it does not report any new PRKN variant.

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) screened 953 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (age at onset 50 years or younger) from 13 movement disorders centers of the CORE-PD study, recruited regardless of family history, for mutations in SNCA, PRKN, PINK1, DJ1, LRRK2, and GBA. In the Results, 33 patients were PRKN heterozygotes and 27 were PRKN homozygotes or compound heterozygotes. The abstract gives 64 (6.7%) PRKN carriers. Hispanic patients were more likely than non-Hispanic patients to carry PRKN mutations (15.6% vs 5.9%, P = 0.003).
quotes: One hundred and fifty eight subjects (16.6%) carried a genetic mutation: 33 were PRKN heterozygotes, and 27 were PRKN homozygotes/compound heterozygotes.
Hispanics were more likely to be PRKN carriers than non-Hispanics (15.6% versus 5.9% p=0.003, Fisher exact test).

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that age at onset was significantly younger in PRKN mutation carriers than in carriers of all other mutations (P < 0.001). Mean age at onset was 29 years in carriers of 2 PRKN mutations and 37 years in PRKN heterozygotes, compared with 42 years in noncarriers. Patients with 2 PRKN mutations made up 35% of cases with onset at age 20 or younger, 17% with onset at 21 to 30 years, and 0.5% with onset at 41 to 50 years.
quotes: AAO was significantly younger among PRKN mutation carriers than among carriers of all other mutations (p <0.001).
Carriers of 2 PRKN mutations | 35% (6) | 17% (8) | 3% (10 | 0.5% (3)

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that PRKN carriers were more likely than LRRK2 carriers to report a family history of PD, even though PRKN-related disease is considered recessive. The authors suggested that the high frequency of PRKN heterozygotes may support the idea that even a single PRKN mutation is a risk factor for early-onset PD.
quotes: PRKN carriers were more likely to report a FHPD than LRRK2 carriers, despite the fact that LRRK2 is autosomal dominant and PRKN is considered a recessive disorder.
Also, the high frequency of PRKN heterozygotes may support the notion that even a single PRKN mutation is a risk of EOPD.

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) described 3 patients with early-onset PD who were heterozygous for a PRKN mutation and also carried a GBA mutation: an exon 2 deletion plus GBA L444P, R275W plus GBA L444P, and D53E plus GBA N370S. A fourth patient, of Jewish ancestry, carried a heterozygous PRKN exon 5-6 deletion together with LRRK2 G2019S. None of these patients reported Parkinson disease in a first-degree relative.
quotes: 3. | PRKN exon 2 deletion heterozygote GBA L444P | Male | no | 34 | 56 | 22 | 20 | 150 | 27 | None
4. | PRKN R275W heterozygote GBA L444P | Female | no | 34 | 48 | 14 | 3 | 500 | 29 | None
7. | PRKN D53E heterozygote GBA N370S | Female | no | 42 | 47 | 5 | 7 | 0 | 30 | None

relevance_reason: This large multicenter cohort of patients with early-onset PD reports how often parkin mutations occur, what kinds are found (including CNVs and Hispanic/Puerto Rican recurrent mutations), and which factors predict carrier status. It adds frequency and genotype-phenotype evidence to the PARK2 entry.

findings.statement: Marder et al. (2010) screened the parkin gene for point mutations and exon copy number variation in 956 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (age at onset younger than 51 years) recruited at 13 movement disorders centers in the CORE-PD study. Sixty-four patients (6.7%) had parkin mutations: 3.9% were heterozygous, 0.6% homozygous, and 2.2% compound heterozygous. Copy number variation was present in 52.3% of mutation carriers (31.6% of heterozygotes, 83.3% of homozygotes, and 81.0% of compound heterozygotes). No consanguinity was reported.
quotes: Sixty-four patients (6.7%) had parkin mutations (3.9% heterozygous, 0.6% homozygous, and 2.2% compound heterozygous).
Copy number variation was present in 52.3% of mutation carriers (31.6% of heterozygous, 83.3% of homozygous, and 81.0% of compound heterozygous).
There was no reported consanguinity.

findings.statement: Marder et al. (2010) found that the prevalence of parkin mutations fell as age at onset rose: 57% (8/14) with onset before age 20, 30% (13/43) at ages 20 to 29, 9% (23/254) at ages 30 to 39, and 3% (20/644) at ages 40 to 50. Every carrier group had a younger mean age at onset than noncarriers (heterozygotes 37.2 years, homozygotes 28.5, compound heterozygotes 28.9, noncarriers 42.0). Compound heterozygotes and homozygotes each had a significantly younger age at onset than heterozygotes. Onset before age 40 was associated with carrying any parkin mutation (OR 5.0), and compared with heterozygotes, younger onset was associated with carrying 2 mutations (OR 6.6).
quotes: The prevalence of mutations declined with AAO from 57% (8/14) in cases with AAO <20, 30% (13/43) in cases with AAO 20–29, 9% (23/254) in cases with AAO 30–39 and 3% (20/644) in those with AAO 40–50 (test for linear trend p<0.001).
Compound heterozygotes and homozygotes each had a significantly younger AAO than heterozygotes.
When those with two mutations were compared to those with a single mutation (heterozygotes), AAO was inversely associated with carrying two mutations (OR 6.6 95%CI 1.6–27.1 p<0.008)

findings.statement: Marder et al. (2010) found that patients with a parkin mutation in the heterozygous state had a younger age at onset than noncarriers after adjustment for ethnicity and family history. The authors concluded that this supports parkin heterozygosity being a susceptibility factor for PD. A family history of PD in a first-degree relative was associated with carrying any parkin mutation (OR 2.8): 11.8% of patients with a family history carried mutations, compared with 5.7% of those without one.
quotes: Our finding that cases with a parkin mutation in the heterozygous state have younger AAO of PD than those who do not have mutations after adjustment for ethnicity and family history of PD supports the concept that parkin heterozygosity is a susceptibility factor for PD.
Among those who reported a family history of PD in a first degree relative, 11.8% carried mutations compared to 5.7% of those who did not have a family history of PD (p=0.007).

findings.statement: In the early-onset PD cohort studied by Marder et al. (2010), dystonia as a presenting sign did not differ between parkin mutation carriers (0%) and noncarriers (1.7%). Response to levodopa was also similar: 93.4% of carriers and 90.5% of noncarriers reported a response to antiparkinson medication.
quotes: Dystonia, as a presenting sign did not differ between carriers (0%) and non-carriers (1.7%) of parkin mutations (p=0.4)
93.4% of carriers compared to 90.5% of non-carriers reported a response to anti-parkinson medications when tried in an adequate does.(p=0.60).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

findings.statement: Marder et al. (2010) found that Hispanic ethnicity was associated with carrying a parkin mutation (15.6% of Hispanic patients vs 5.7% of white non-Hispanic patients; OR 2.7). None of the 12 Black non-Hispanic patients carried a mutation. Of the 12 Hispanic carriers, 7 were Puerto Rican. Six Hispanic patients (5 Puerto Rican and 1 Mexican) carried a deletion of exons 3-4, and both exon 3-4 homozygotes were of Puerto Rican descent. The second most common mutation in Hispanics was 255delA, found in 3 Puerto Ricans together with the exon 3-4 deletion and in 1 Mexican heterozygote; it was not detected in 139 Caribbean Hispanic controls.
quotes: None of 12 Black non-Hispanics carried a parkin mutation, while 5.7% (48/838) White non-Hispanic, 15.6% (12/77) of Hispanics and 14.8 (4/27) of cases in “other” ethnic groups combined did (p<0.002).
Six cases (5 Puerto Rican and one Mexican carried deletions of exon 3–4. Both exon 3–4 homozygotes were of Puerto Rican descent.
The second most common mutation in Hispanics was 255delA, present in three Puerto Ricans in association with the exon 3–4 deletion and one Mexican heterozygote.

findings.statement: Among the compound heterozygotes, Marder et al. (2010) identified recurrent combinations including 255delA plus an exon 3-4 deletion (3 Hispanic patients) and Arg275Trp with a variety of second alleles. Arg275Trp was also the most frequent heterozygous mutation, found in 8 patients. Other mutations found included Arg42Pro, Gly430Asp, and an exon 3 40-bp deletion.
quotes: 7 | Arg275Trp | Point/missense | RING1 | heterozygote | White (6), Hispanic(1), other (1)
2 and 3–4 | 255delA+exon 3–4 deletion | Small nucleotide deletion/insertion, CNV | Ubiquitin | Comp het | Hispanic (3)
7 and 12 | Arg275Trp + Gly430Asp | Point/missense | RING1, RING2 | Comp het | White (1)

relevance_reason: Functional study of mitochondrial function and morphology in fibroblasts from 5 patients with biallelic parkin mutations and early-onset parkinsonism, with siRNA knockdown and pharmacological rescue.

findings.statement: Mortiboys et al. (2008) studied skin fibroblasts from 5 patients with early-onset parkinsonism and homozygous or compound heterozygous parkin mutations, identified by direct sequencing and MLPA gene dosage analysis. Genotypes included 255delA with exon 5 deletion; homozygous 202_203delAG (exon 2); 202_203delAG with exon 2 deletion; 202_203delAG with exon 4 deletion; and c.101-102delAG (p.Gln34ArgfsX38) with c.1289G>A (p.Gly430Asp).
quotes: Punch skin biopsies were taken from five patients with homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the parkin gene following routine clinical procedures.
Patient 2 | 202_203delAG ( exon 2) | 202_203delAG ( exon 2)
Patient 5 | c.101-102delAG p.Gln34ArgfsX38 | c.1289G<A p.Gly430Asp

findings.statement: Mortiboys et al. (2008) found that fibroblasts from 5 parkin-mutant patients had mitochondrial membrane potential reduced by about 30% in glucose medium and 70% in galactose medium, complex I activity reduced by about 42%, with normal complex III and IV activity, reduced complex I-linked (but not complex II-linked) ATP production, and a 58% reduction in cellular ATP levels. Cell viability and growth were unaffected.
quotes: Mitochondrial membrane potential was lower in all 5 parkin mutant fibroblast cultures by an average of 30% (Fig. 1A; p < 0.01).
complex I activity was lower by an average of 42% in parkin mutant fibroblasts compared to controls (Fig. 1B; p < 0.005).
The lower complex I-linked ATP production also results in an overall decrease of cellular ATP levels by 58% in the parkin mutant fibroblasts (Fig. 2C; p < 0.05).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

findings.statement: Mortiboys et al. (2008) observed increased mitochondrial branching in parkin-mutant fibroblasts, which correlated with lower complex I-linked ATP production and lower complex I activity, suggesting that the functional and morphological effects of parkin deficiency on mitochondria are related. FRAP assays showed reduced functional connectivity of the mitochondrial matrix, worsened by rotenone, and rotenone shortened mitochondria in parkin-mutant but not control cells.
quotes: The lower complex I linked ATP production correlates with an increase in both the degree of mitochondrial branching (form factor, R2 = 0.903, p < 0.001; Fig 3E)
This indicates that the functional and morphological effects of parkin deficiency on mitochondria are related to each other.
Overall, these results show that parkin deficient fibroblasts have a basal defect in functional connectivity that is enhanced by rotenone.

findings.statement: Mortiboys et al. (2008) showed that siRNA knockdown of parkin by 80% in control fibroblasts reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and cellular ATP and increased mitochondrial branching by 70%, indicating that parkin deficiency is sufficient to explain the patient cell defects. In contrast, 50% knockdown, mimicking haploinsufficiency, had no effect, which the authors considered consistent with true recessive inheritance and not supportive of heterozygosity as a PD risk factor.
quotes: The siRNA mediated parkin knockdown data therefore show that parkin deficiency is sufficient to explain the mitochondrial deficiencies seen in the patient fibroblasts.

In contrast, 50% knockdown of parkin, mimicking haploinsufficiency in human patient tissue, did not result in impaired mitochondrial transmembrane potential or alteration of mitochondrial morphology (Fig. 4E+F).
This is consistent with true recessive inheritance and would not support the concept that heterozygosity for parkin is a risk factor for PD.

findings.statement: Mortiboys et al. (2008) found that treatment of parkin-mutant fibroblasts with the glutathione precursor OTCA (10 microM) restored mitochondrial membrane potential to 95% of control levels and completely restored cellular ATP, apparently via a compensatory increase in complex II activity rather than correction of the complex I defect; glutathione methyl ester gave only partial rescue (60%). They suggested patient fibroblasts could serve as a screening system for disease-modifying compounds.
quotes: Treatment of all 5 parkin mutant fibroblasts with 10μM OTCA showed improvements of mitochondrial membrane potential in every individual patient, with the average membrane potential being restored to 95% of control levels (Fig. 7B).
This suggests that the observed rescue effect of mitochondrial membrane potential is due to a compensatory increase in complex II activity rather than a rescue of the complex I defect.

relevance_reason: Estimates the penetrance of PD in carriers of parkin mutations (including heterozygotes) using a kin-cohort study of early-onset PD probands. This bears on inheritance and penetrance in PARK2.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2008) screened the Parkin gene for point mutations and exon deletions and duplications in 247 probands with Parkinson disease (onset at or before age 50 years) and 104 control probands enrolled in the Genetic Epidemiology of Parkinson's Disease (GEPD) study. They found Parkin mutations in 25 probands with PD (10.1%). Eighteen of these 25 (72.0%) were heterozygotes, and 1 Parkin homozygote was reported in 2 sibs with PD.
quotes: We assessed point mutations and exon deletions and duplications in the Parkin gene in 247 probands with PD (age at onset < or =50 years) and 104 control probands
Parkin mutations were identified in 25 probands with PD (10.1%), 18 (72.0%) of whom were heterozygotes. One Parkin homozygote was reported in 2 siblings with PD.

phenotypes.text: Parkinson disease with onset at or before 50 years

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2008) used the kin-cohort method to estimate the cumulative incidence of PD to age 65 years in first-degree relatives who carried Parkin mutations (age-specific penetrance). The estimate was 7.0% (95% CI, 0.4-71.9%), compared with 1.7% in noncarrier relatives of cases (P = 0.59) and 1.1% in relatives of controls. They concluded that the risk in noncarrier relatives of early-onset cases was not significantly greater than the general population risk among controls, and that age-specific penetrance among Parkin carriers, particularly heterozygotes, deserved further study.
quotes: The cumulative incidence of PD to age 65 years in carrier relatives (age-specific penetrance) was estimated to be 7.0% (95% confidence interval, 0.4%-71.9%), compared with 1.7% (95% confidence interval, 0.8%-3.4%) in noncarrier relatives of the cases (P = .59)
Age-specific penetrance among Parkin carriers, in particular heterozygotes, deserves further study.

relevance_reason: Large case-control sequencing study of parkin showing heterozygous point mutations are equally frequent in controls and PD patients; relevant to interpretation of heterozygous PARK2 variants.

findings.statement: Kay et al. (2007) sequenced the parkin gene in 302 patients with Parkinson disease and 301 control subjects, with replication in 1,260 additional patients and 1,657 control subjects. They detected 34 variants, 21 of them novel; 12 were polymorphisms and 22 were rare variants. Patients and controls did not differ in the frequency, type, or functional location of the variants.
quotes: A total of 302 patients and 301 control subjects were sequenced, and findings were replicated in 1,260 additional patients and 1,657 control subjects.

Thirty-four variants were detected, of which 21 were novel; 12 were polymorphisms and 22 were rare variants. Patients and control subjects did not differ in the frequency, type, or functional location of the variants.

findings.statement: Kay et al. (2007) found the P437L parkin variant, a common mutation thought to be pathogenic, in unaffected control subjects.
quotes: Even P437L, a common mutation thought to be pathogenic, was present in unaffected control subjects.

findings.statement: Kay et al. (2007) concluded that parkin point mutations are not exclusive to Parkinson disease and that a single point mutation in a patient, in the absence of a second mutation, should not be taken as a cause of disease unless corroborated by family data and functional studies. Their study did not support heterozygous parkin sequence variants as risk factors for PD; whether heterozygous dosage anomalies are associated with PD remained to be determined.
quotes: parkin point mutations are not exclusive to PD. The mere presence of a single point mutation in a patient, in the absence of a second mutation, should not be taken as a cause of disease unless corroborated by family data and functional studies.

This study does not support the notion that heterozygous parkin sequence variants (mutations or polymorphisms) are risk factors for PD. Whether heterozygous dosage anomalies are associated with PD remains to be determined.

relevance_reason: Reports a large consanguineous Brazilian kindred with early-onset PD caused by a novel homozygous parkin splice-site mutation, with segregation and transcript analysis.

findings.statement: Chien et al. (2006) described a genetic isolate from north-eastern Brazil in which genealogical studies connected 255 individuals, 15 of whom had Parkinson disease. DNA was obtained from 10 early-onset PD patients, 1 case with likely neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism, and 15 unaffected relatives. The average age at onset of PD symptoms was 30.8 years (range, 12 to 46 years).
quotes: Genealogical studies could connect 255 individuals, of whom 15 had PD.
The average age at onset of PD symptoms was 30.8 years (range 12-46).

findings.statement: Chien et al. (2006) noted that geographic isolation and multiple consanguineous marriages in the Brazilian kindred initially suggested autosomal recessive inheritance, and haplotype analysis revealed homozygosity in the PD patients for markers across the PARK2 locus.
quotes: Geographic isolation and multiple consanguineous marriages initially suggested an autosomal recessive inheritance for PD in these patients.
Haplotype analysis revealed homozygosity in the PD patients for markers across the PARK2 locus.

findings.statement: In 10 patients with early-onset PD from a Brazilian genetic isolate, Chien et al. (2006) identified a novel homozygous splice-site mutation in the parkin gene (IVS1+1G-T) that completely cosegregated with the phenotype. cDNA analysis showed total loss of parkin transcript in homozygous carriers, indicating a loss-of-function mutation.
quotes: Genomic sequencing identified a novel homozygous splice-site parkin mutation (IVS1 + 1G/T), which completely co-segregated with the early-onset PD phenotype.
cDNA analysis confirmed the total loss of parkin transcript in homozygous mutation carriers, delineating this as a loss-of-function mutation.

findings.statement: Chien et al. (2006) found that the case with neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism and 13 of 15 healthy relatives were heterozygous carriers of the IVS1+1G-T parkin mutation. The absence of PD in heterozygotes indicated a genuinely recessive mutation, suggesting that parkin haploinsufficiency is not a relevant risk factor for early- or late-onset PD, although the authors suggested it could facilitate neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism.
quotes: The case with neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism and 13 of 15 healthy relatives were heterozygous carriers of the mutation.

The absence of PD in heterozygous carriers indicates a genuinely recessive nature of this mutation, suggesting that parkin haploinsufficiency is not a relevant risk factor for early- or late-onset PD.
However, parkin haploinsufficiency could facilitate the emergence of neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism.

relevance_reason: This paper reports a large pedigree with Parkin (PRKN) mutation carriers. It includes clinical, genetic and neuropathological data (Lewy bodies) for compound heterozygous patients.

findings.statement: Pramstaller et al. (2005) reported a 7-generation pedigree of 196 individuals, 25 of whom had levodopa-responsive parkinsonism. Parkin mutations were found in 77 subjects. Of the 25 patients, 5 carried compound heterozygous mutations and met UK PD Society Brain Bank criteria for definite Parkinson disease. Eight carried only a heterozygous Parkin mutation, 7 had no Parkin mutation, and the status of 5 deceased patients was unknown.
quotes: We report the clinical, genetic, and neuropathological findings of a seven generation-spanning pedigree with 196 individuals, 25 of whom had levodopa-responsive parkinsonism. Genetic analyses indicated Parkin mutations in 77 subjects.

Among the 25 patients, 5 carried compound heterozygous mutations and met criteria for definite Parkinson's disease (PD) according to UK PD Society Brain Bank guidelines; 8 subjects carried only a heterozygous Parkin mutation.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

findings.statement: In this pedigree, Pramstaller et al. (2005) found that age at onset differed significantly between patients with compound heterozygous Parkin mutations and both heterozygous carriers and patients without detectable Parkin mutations. The authors suggested the pedigree offered a chance to study heterozygous Parkin mutations as a risk factor for PD.
quotes: Survival analyses showed a significant difference in the age-at-onset distribution between patients with compound heterozygous mutations and the groups of heterozygous carriers and subjects without detectable Parkin mutations.
This large Parkin pedigree represents a unique opportunity to prospectively study the role of heterozygous Parkin mutations as a PD risk factor

findings.statement: Pramstaller et al. (2005) identified compound heterozygous Parkin mutations, a deletion of exon 7 and del1072T, in a 73-year-old patient from the large pedigree. Both mutations deleted the In-Between-RING (IBR) domain.
quotes: Autopsy of a 73-year-old patient, who carried two mutant Parkin alleles (delExon7 + del1072T)
In-Between-RING ("IBR") domain, which had been deleted by both mutations

findings.statement: In a 73-year-old compound heterozygous Parkin mutation carrier, Pramstaller et al. (2005) found at autopsy PD-type cell loss, reactive gliosis, and alpha-synuclein-positive Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra and locus ceruleus. Surviving neurons reacted with antibodies to the Parkin N terminus but not to the IBR domain.
quotes: showed PD-type cell loss, reactive gliosis, and alpha-synuclein-positive Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra and locus ceruleus
Surviving neurons were reactive with antibodies to the N terminus of Parkin but not the In-Between-RING ("IBR") domain

phenotypes.text: Lewy bodies in substantia nigra and locus ceruleus

relevance_reason: Reports a clinical/electrophysiologic feature (reduced sural SNAP amplitude, sensory axonal neuropathy) in PARK2 patients.

findings.statement: Ohsawa et al. (2005) performed nerve conduction studies in 9 PARK2 patients and 8 patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease and found a significant reduction of sural sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitude in 8 of the PARK2 patients, most of whom were asymptomatic. The authors suggested that sensory axonal neuropathy may be a common clinical feature of PARK2.
quotes: The authors performed nerve conduction studies in nine PARK2 and eight idiopathic Parkinson disease patients and found a significant reduction of sural sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitude in eight PARK2 patients who mostly remained asymptomatic.
These data suggest that sensory axonal neuropathy may be a common clinical feature of PARK2

phenotypes.text: reduced sural sensory nerve action potential amplitude
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased amplitude of sensory action potentials

findings.statement: Ohsawa et al. (2005) suggested that a reduced amplitude of the sural SNAP could be a diagnostic indicator of PARK2.
quotes: a reduced amplitude of sural SNAP could be a diagnostic indicator of PARK2

relevance_reason: The paper's PET study shows dopaminergic dysfunction in people who carry one parkin mutation but have no symptoms. This bears on heterozygote risk in PARK2.

findings.statement: Khan et al. (2005) used 18F-dopa PET to study 13 unrelated asymptomatic heterozygous carriers of a single parkin mutation. Compared with control subjects, the carriers had significantly reduced 18F-dopa uptake in the caudate, putamen, and ventral and dorsal midbrain. Four of the carriers had subtle extrapyramidal signs.
quotes: The authors used 18F-dopa PET to study 13 asymptomatic parkin heterozygotes and found a significant reduction of (18)F-dopa uptake in caudate, putamen, ventral, and dorsal midbrain compared with control subjects.
Four had subtle extrapyramidal signs.

findings.statement: Khan et al. (2005) concluded that being heterozygous for a parkin mutation is a risk factor for nigrostriatal dysfunction. They suggested that in some carriers it may contribute to late-onset Parkinson disease, even though parkin disease is usually autosomal recessive.
quotes: Parkin heterozygosity is a risk factor for nigrostriatal dysfunction and in some may contribute to late-onset Parkinson disease.
Parkin disease is usually autosomal recessive; however, two studies have shown that asymptomatic heterozygotes have nigrostriatal dysfunction

relevance_reason: Autopsy case report of a PARK2 (parkin) patient with a homozygous exon 3 deletion, describing the neuropathology, including alpha-synuclein-positive inclusions.

findings.statement: Sasaki et al. (2004) reported autopsy findings in a patient with autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism. Brain lesions were limited to dopaminergic neuron systems such as the substantia nigra and locus ceruleus. Melanin-containing neurons in the pars compacta of the substantia nigra were moderately to severely depleted, with gliosis. Neurons in the locus ceruleus were mildly decreased, and melanin pigment was seen outside neurons.
quotes: Histologically, the lesions of the brain were limited to the dopaminergic neuron system such as the substantia nigra (SN) and locus ceruleus.
Melanin-containing neurons in the pars compacta of the SN were moderately to severely depleted, accompanied by gliosis.
In the locus ceruleus, neurons were mildly decreased and extraneuronal melanin pigments were seen.

phenotypes.text: depletion of melanin-containing neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta
mild neuronal loss in locus ceruleus
phenotypes.hpo_label: Neuronal loss in central nervous system

findings.statement: Sasaki et al. (2004) found no Lewy bodies in the neuropil of the substantia nigra pars compacta or the locus ceruleus. Basophilic inclusion bodies were seen only occasionally, in the neuropil of the pedunculopontine nucleus. These inclusions were doughnut-shaped or round and stained positive for alpha-synuclein and ubiquitin. The authors concluded that different parkin gene abnormalities may lead to differences in the degree and distribution of neuronal degeneration, including whether Lewy bodies are present. They also suggested that parkin-induced parkinsonism may be related to idiopathic Parkinson disease.
quotes: Lewy bodies were not observed in the neuropils of the pars compacta of the SN or locus ceruleus. However, basophilic inclusion bodies were only occasionally observed in the neuropils of the pedunculopontine nucleus in the mesencephalic reticular formation.

Immunohistochemistry with antibodies to alpha-synuclein and ubiquitin showed alpha-synuclein- and ubiquitin-positive inclusions in the neuropils of the pedunculopontine nucleus, which had a doughnut or round shape.

A variety of parkin gene abnormalities may produce pathologic differences in the degree and distribution of neuronal degeneration, including the absence or presence of Lewy bodies. A relationship between parkin-induced parkinsonism and idiopathic Parkinson disease (PD) may exist.

phenotypes.text: Lewy bodies in substantia nigra and locus ceruleus
alpha-synuclein- and ubiquitin-positive inclusions in pedunculopontine nucleus

findings.statement: Sasaki et al. (2004) reported that their autopsied patient with autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism carried a homozygous deletion of exon 3 in the parkin gene.
quotes: To report an autopsy case of an autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism patient with a homozygous exon 3 deletion in the parkin gene and alpha-synuclein-positive inclusions.

relevance_reason: Clinic-based screening of parkin in early-onset PD; reports mutation frequency, types (exon deletions/duplications, P437L, R402W), compound heterozygous vs heterozygous cases, and phenotype comparison.

findings.statement: Poorkaj et al. (2004) screened all 12 exons of the parkin gene by sequencing and dosage analysis in 39 movement disorder clinic patients with PD onset at or before 40 years of age and found mutations in 7 patients: 2 were compound heterozygous and 5 were heterozygous. Mutations included deletions of exons 2, 3, and 8, duplications of exons 2-4 and 9, and a P437L substitution; 78% of mutations were deletions/multiplications. None of the point mutations found in patients were detected in 96 controls.
quotes: Mutations were found in 7/39 patients. Two patients were compound heterozygous; five were heterozygous.
Mutations included deletions in exons 2, 3, and 8, duplications in exons 2-4, and 9, and P437L substitution. Seventy-eight percent of mutations were deletions/multiplications.
None of the point mutations found in patients were detected in 96 controls.

findings.statement: Poorkaj et al. (2004) found a novel parkin substitution, R402W, in 1 patient with early-onset PD and in 1 control.
quotes: A novel substitution (R402W) was found in one patient and in one control.

findings.statement: Poorkaj et al. (2004) found that phenotypes of parkin mutation carriers were consistent with idiopathic PD, so that parkin cases could present as typical idiopathic PD distinguishable only by molecular testing.
quotes: parkin phenotypes were consistent with idiopathic PD.
parkin cases can present as typical idiopathic PD, distinguishable only by molecular testing.

findings.statement: Poorkaj et al. (2004) found that in the clinic setting 10% of PD patients had early-onset disease and 18% of these had parkin mutations, but if parkin is recessive only 5% of early-onset cases, those with compound mutations, could be attributed to this locus. The mutation frequency was 0.12 (95% CI 0.04-0.19), and 70% of parkin cases were heterozygous; the authors stated that it was unclear whether heterozygous mutations are pathogenic.
quotes: 10% of PD patients had early-onset and 18% of them had parkin mutations. However, if parkin is recessive, only 5% of early-onset cases who had compound mutations could be attributed to this locus.
Mutation frequency was 0.12 (95% CI 0.04-0.19).
Seventy percent of parkin cases were heterozygous. It is unclear whether heterozygous mutations are pathogenic.

findings.statement: Poorkaj et al. (2004) concluded that parkin-based diagnosis and counseling require a better understanding of the mode of inheritance, penetrance, and carrier frequencies.
quotes: parkin-based diagnosis and counseling require a better understanding of the mode of inheritance, penetrance, and carrier frequencies.

relevance_reason: Large genotype-phenotype comparison of early-onset parkinsonism patients with and without parkin mutations; directly characterises PARK2 phenotype and genotype-phenotype correlations.

findings.statement: Lohmann et al. (2003) compared the phenotype of 146 patients with early-onset parkinsonism carrying parkin mutations with that of 250 patients without parkin mutations. Although no single sign distinguished the groups, patients with mutations had significantly earlier and more symmetrical onset, dystonia more often at onset, hyperreflexia, slower disease progression, and a tendency toward a greater response to levodopa despite lower doses.
quotes: we have compared the phenotype of a large series of 146 patients with and 250 patients without parkin mutations

Although no single sign distinguished the groups, patients with mutations had significantly earlier and more symmetrical onset, dystonia more often at onset and hyperreflexia, slower progression of the disease, and a tendency toward a greater response to levodopa despite lower doses.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

findings.statement: Lohmann et al. (2003) found by forward stepwise multiple logistic regression that dystonia at onset and brisk reflexes were no longer significantly different between parkin carriers and noncarriers but correlated with age at onset rather than with parkin mutation status. Among parkin mutation carriers, age at onset varied, as did rate of progression: the younger the age at onset, the slower the evolution.
quotes: After forward stepwise multiple logistic regression analysis, dystonia at onset and brisk reflexes were not longer significantly different but were correlated with age at onset rather than the presence of the parkin mutation.
Age at onset in carriers of parkin mutations varied as did the rate of progression of the disease: the younger the age at onset the slower the evolution.

findings.statement: Lohmann et al. (2003) found that carriers of at least one parkin missense mutation had a higher UPDRS motor score than those carrying two truncating mutations, and that missense mutations in functional domains of parkin resulted in earlier onset.
quotes: carriers of at least one missense mutation had a higher United Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale motor score than those carrying two truncating mutations
missense mutations in functional domains of parkin resulted in earlier onset

findings.statement: Lohmann et al. (2003) found that patients with a single heterozygous parkin mutation had significantly later and more asymmetrical onset and more frequent levodopa-induced fluctuations and dystonia than patients with two mutations.
quotes: Patients with a single heterozygous mutation had significantly later and more asymmetrical onset and more frequent levodopa-induced fluctuations and dystonia than patients with two mutations.

relevance_reason: The paper screened Parkin (PARK2) for mutations in families with early- and late-onset Parkinson disease. It gives mutation frequencies and age-at-onset ranges, and it suggests that heterozygous exon 7 mutations act as susceptibility alleles for late-onset PD.

findings.statement: Oliveira et al. (2003) noted that they had previously detected linkage of idiopathic Parkinson disease to the chromosome 6 region containing the Parkin gene (D6S305, lod score 5.47) in families with at least one subject with age at onset younger than 40 years.
quotes: Previously, we detected linkage of idiopathic PD to the region on chromosome 6 containing the Parkin gene (D6S305, logarithm of odds score, 5.47) in families with at least one subject with age at onset (AAO) younger than 40 years.

findings.statement: Oliveira et al. (2003) screened the Parkin gene in 174 multiplex families from a genomic screen and in 133 additional Parkinson disease families. They found mutations in 18% of early-onset families and 2% of late-onset families (5% of all families screened). Age at onset in patients with Parkin mutations ranged from 12 to 71 years. Excluding exon 7 mutations, the mean age at onset was 31.5 years.
quotes: Mutation analysis of the Parkin gene in the 174 multiplex families from the genomic screen and 133 additional PD families identified mutations in 18% of early-onset and 2% of late-onset families (5% of total families screened).
The AAO of patients with Parkin mutations ranged from 12 to 71 years. Excluding exon 7 mutations, the mean AAO of patients with Parkin mutations was 31.5 years.

findings.statement: Oliveira et al. (2003) found that mutations in Parkin exon 7, the first RING finger (cys253 to trp, arg256 to cys, arg275 to trp, and asp280 to asn), occurred mainly in heterozygous Parkinson disease patients with a much later age at onset (mean 49.2 years). These mutations were not found in controls in this study or in several previous reports (920 chromosomes). The authors suggested that heterozygous Parkin mutations, especially those in exon 7, act as susceptibility alleles for late-onset Parkinson disease.
quotes: mutations in exon 7, the first RING finger (Cys253Trp, Arg256Cys, Arg275Trp, and Asp280Asn) were observed primarily in heterozygous PD patients with a much later AAO (mean AAO, 49.2 years) but were not found in controls in this study or several previous reports (920 chromosomes).

These findings suggest that mutations in Parkin contribute to the common form of PD and that heterozygous mutations, especially those lying in exon 7, act as susceptibility alleles for late-onset form of Parkinson disease.

relevance_reason: Screened parkin in families with multiple affected siblings who have PD. Found parkin mutations, including single heterozygous mutations, in patients whose PD began later in life. This adds to genotype-phenotype data for PARK2.

findings.statement: Foroud et al. (2003) screened the parkin gene by quantitative PCR and exon sequencing in families with at least 2 sibs with PD. The families screened had either early-onset PD (onset at or before age 50 years) or a positive lod score with a marker in parkin intron 7. They identified 25 different parkin mutations in 103 individuals from 47 families. Forty-one individuals had mutations in both parkin alleles, and 62 had a single mutation in only 1 allele.
quotes: Families with at least two siblings with PD were ascertained to identify genes contributing to PD susceptibility.

A total of 25 different mutations in the parkin gene were identified in 103 individuals from 47 families. Mutations were found in both parkin alleles in 41 of the individuals, whereas a single mutation in only one of the two parkin alleles was observed in 62 individuals.

findings.statement: Of the 103 individuals with parkin mutations reported by Foroud et al. (2003), 35 (34%) had onset of PD at age 60 years or older. Thirty of these 35 (86%) had a detectable mutation on only 1 parkin allele. The authors concluded that parkin mutations occur in familial PD with older onset, and that heterozygosity for a parkin mutation leads to later-onset PD. Few significant clinical differences were seen among individuals with 2, 1, or no mutated parkin copies.
quotes: Thirty-five of the subjects (34%) with a parkin mutation had an age at onset of 60 years or above with 30 of these 35 (86%) having a detectable mutation on only one parkin allele.
Few significant clinical differences were observed among individuals with two, one, or no mutated copies of the parkin gene.
Mutations in the parkin gene occur among individuals with PD with an older age at onset (> or =60 years) who have a positive family history of the disease.

relevance_reason: Mutation screen of Spanish families with familial PD that identifies PARK2 mutations, including novel variants, in families with recessive inheritance, along with symptomatic heterozygous carriers.

findings.statement: Hoenicka et al. (2002) studied 19 Spanish kindreds with familial Parkinson disease: 13 with recessive inheritance, 4 with dominant inheritance and 2 with uncertain inheritance. Using SSCP, direct sequencing and restriction digestion of PCR-amplified genomic DNA, they found 5 different parkin (Park2) mutations in 5 of the 13 recessive families. These were deletions of exons 3 and 5, 225delA, and the novel mutations V56E and C212Y. The authors concluded that Park2 mutations account for 38% of families with recessive parkinsonism in Spain.
quotes: To analyze the clinical and molecular data of 19 Spanish kindreds (13 with recessive, 4 with dominant, and 2 with uncertain inheritance) who have familial Parkinson disease.
We found 5 different mutations in Park2 gene in 5 of the families with recessive inheritance.
Mutations in Park2 gene account for 38% of the families with recessive parkinsonism in Spain.

findings.statement: In Spanish families with autosomal recessive Parkinson disease, Hoenicka et al. (2002) identified a previously unreported Park2 missense mutation, V56E.
quotes: To our knowledge, 2 of these mutations, V56E and C212Y, have not been previously reported.

findings.statement: In Spanish families with autosomal recessive Parkinson disease, Hoenicka et al. (2002) identified a previously unreported Park2 missense mutation, C212Y.
quotes: To our knowledge, 2 of these mutations, V56E and C212Y, have not been previously reported.

findings.statement: Hoenicka et al. (2002) found that heterozygous carriers of a single Park2 mutation were either asymptomatic or developed symptoms in late adulthood or after brief exposure to haloperidol. Two simple heterozygous carriers were symptomatic. The authors suggested that heterozygous mutations could be a risk factor for parkinsonism.
quotes: Heterozygous carriers of a single Park2 mutation either were asymptomatic or developed clinical symptoms in late adulthood or after brief exposure to haloperidol therapy.
We found 2 cases of simple heterozygous Park2 mutation carriers that developed clinical symptoms, either in late adulthood or after brief exposure to parkinsonizing agents.
heterozygous mutations could be a risk factor for parkinsonism

findings.statement: Hoenicka et al. (2002) found no previously described alpha-synuclein (Park1) or UCHL1 (Park5) mutations in any of the 19 Spanish families with familial Parkinson disease.
quotes: None of these families have either Park1 or Park5 mutations.

relevance_reason: Reports parkin mutations (40-bp exon 3 deletion, R275W) in early-onset parkinsonism families, including an autopsy that found Lewy bodies.

findings.statement: Farrer et al. (2001) sequenced the parkin gene in 38 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (onset before age 41 years) and followed up 2 probands with mutations. Haplotype analysis of the 2 families showed a shared chromosome 6 carrying a novel 40-bp deletion in exon 3, which cosegregated with disease.
quotes: We have sequenced the parkin gene of 38 patients with early-onset Parkinson's disease (<41 years). Two probands with mutations were followed up.
Haplotype analysis of these families revealed a common chromosome 6, with a novel 40 bp exon 3 deletion that cosegregated with disease.

findings.statement: Farrer et al. (2001) found that the proband of the smaller kindred carried an R275W substitution in exon 7 of the parkin gene along with the 40-bp exon 3 deletion. RNA analysis showed that the 2 mutations were on different transcripts, consistent with compound heterozygosity.
quotes: In the proband of the smaller kindred, an exon 7 R275W substitution was identified in addition to the exon 3 deletion; RNA analysis demonstrated that the mutations were on alternate transcripts.

findings.statement: Farrer et al. (2001) found Lewy body pathology typical of idiopathic Parkinson disease at autopsy in the compound heterozygous proband from the smaller kindred. Classically, parkin-related disease had been associated with loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and locus ceruleus without Lewy bodies.
quotes: However, Lewy body pathology typical of idiopathic Parkinson's disease was found at autopsy in the proband from the smaller kindred.
Classically, this disease has been associated with loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta and locus ceruleus, without Lewy body pathology.

findings.statement: Farrer et al. (2001) suggested that compound heterozygous parkin mutations and loss of parkin protein may lead to early-onset parkinsonism with Lewy body pathology. They also suggested that a hemizygous (single heterozygous) mutation may increase susceptibility to typical Parkinson disease.
quotes: These data suggest that compound heterozygous parkin mutations and loss of parkin protein may lead to early-onset parkinsonism with Lewy body pathology, while a hemizygous mutation may confer increased susceptibility to typical Parkinson's disease.

relevance_reason: The paper reports an Italian family with parkin gene mutations (an exon 2 triplication and exon 3-4 deletions) in which inheritance looked dominant but was recessive. It directly describes the PARK2 phenotype and its inheritance.

findings.statement: Lücking et al. (2001) reported an Italian family in which parkinsonism caused by parkin gene mutations showed pseudo-dominant inheritance. The affected father was homozygous for a parkin mutation, the unaffected mother was a heterozygous carrier, and their affected son was a compound heterozygote. The authors concluded that pseudo-dominant inheritance of parkin mutations has to be considered in early-onset parkinsonism.
quotes: The authors report an Italian family with pseudo-dominant inheritance of parkinsonism attributable to parkin gene mutations.
Thus, pseudo-dominant inheritance of parkin gene mutations has to be considered in early-onset parkinsonism

findings.statement: In the Italian family reported by Lücking et al. (2001), the father developed parkinsonism at age 57 years and his son at age 31 years.
quotes: The father (disease onset at age 57 years) was homozygous for a triplication of exon 2 that is so far unique.
the son (onset at age 31 years) was a compound heterozygote carrying both mutations

findings.statement: In an Italian family, Lücking et al. (2001) found that the affected father was homozygous for a triplication of parkin exon 2, a mutation the authors described as so far unique. His affected son was compound heterozygous for this triplication and for a deletion of exons 3 and 4. The authors recommended sensitive screening methods such as semiquantitative multiplex PCR.
quotes: The father (disease onset at age 57 years) was homozygous for a triplication of exon 2 that is so far unique.
sensitive screening techniques, such as semiquantitative multiplex PCR, should be applied

findings.statement: Lücking et al. (2001) found that the unaffected mother in an Italian family was heterozygous for a deletion of parkin exons 3 and 4. Her affected son was compound heterozygous for this deletion and for the paternal exon 2 triplication.
quotes: The unaffected mother was heterozygous for deletions of exons 3 and 4, and the son (onset at age 31 years) was a compound heterozygote carrying both mutations.

relevance_reason: The paper screened PARKIN in patients with early-onset parkinsonism and found point mutations along with exon deletions and duplications.

findings.statement: Hedrich et al. (2001) screened the parkin gene in 21 patients with early-onset parkinsonism. Conventional screening by SSCP and sequence analysis found 3 mutations: a single base pair substitution in exon 3 and small deletions in exon 9.
quotes: In 21 patients with EOP, three mutations (a single base pair substitution in exon 3 and small deletions in exon 9) were detected by conventional mutational screening (single-strand conformation polymorphism and sequence analysis)

variants.as_reported: single base pair substitution in exon 3

findings.statement: Hedrich et al. (2001) used quantitative duplex real-time PCR to find parkin gene dosage changes in 7 of 21 patients with early-onset parkinsonism. These included heterozygous and compound heterozygous deletions of exons 2, 3, 5, and 7, a homozygous exon 7 deletion, and 2 heterozygous duplications of exon 4. Two patients carried more than 2 parkin mutations.
quotes: alterations of gene dosage were found in seven patients

We identified heterozygous and compound heterozygous deletions of exons 2, 3, 5 and 7. The latter was also found in the homozygous state. In addition, two heterozygous duplications of exon 4 were observed.
Remarkably, two patients carried more than two parkin mutations.

findings.statement: Hedrich et al. (2001) concluded that mutation analysis of the parkin gene should include gene dosage studies. They developed a real-time kinetic quantitative duplex PCR method, using fluorescence resonance energy transfer on the LightCycler, to screen all 12 parkin exons for deletions and duplications.
quotes: we developed a new method of quantitative duplex PCR using the fluorescence resonance energy transfer technique on the LightCycler (Roche Diagnostics)

This is the first study systematically screening all 12 exons of parkin by real-time, kinetic quantification and clearly shows that mutational analysis of the parkin gene should include gene dosage studies.

relevance_reason: This functional study of the parkin–alpha-synuclein interaction in human brain shows that mutant parkin from autosomal recessive PD fails to bind and ubiquitinate alphaSp22, and that alphaSp22 builds up in parkin-deficient brains. That is evidence about how the disease arises.

findings.statement: Shimura et al. (2001) identified a protein complex in normal human brain made up of parkin as the E3 ubiquitin ligase, UbcH7 as its associated E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, and a new 22-kD glycosylated form of alpha-synuclein (alphaSp22) as its substrate. In an in vitro ubiquitination assay, normal parkin converted alphaSp22 into polyubiquitinated, high molecular weight species.
quotes: We have now identified a protein complex in normal human brain that includes parkin as the E3 ubiquitin ligase, UbcH7 as its associated E2 ubiquitin conjugating enzyme, and a new 22-kilodalton glycosylated form of alpha-synuclein (alphaSp22) as its substrate.
In an in vitro ubiquitination assay, alphaSp22 was modified by normal but not mutant parkin into polyubiquitinated, high molecular weight species.

findings.statement: Shimura et al. (2001) found that, unlike normal parkin, mutant parkin associated with autosomal recessive PD did not bind alphaSp22 and did not ubiquitinate it. In parkin-deficient PD brains, alphaSp22 accumulated in a non-ubiquitinated form. The authors concluded that loss of parkin function causes pathological accumulation of alphaSp22, and suggested that this reaction underlies the accumulation of ubiquitinated alpha-synuclein in conventional PD.
quotes: In contrast to normal parkin, mutant parkin associated with autosomal recessive PD failed to bind alphaSp22.
Accordingly, alphaSp22 accumulated in a non-ubiquitinated form in parkin-deficient PD brains.
We conclude that alphaSp22 is a substrate for parkin's ubiquitin ligase activity in normal human brain and that loss of parkin function causes pathological alphaSp22 accumulation.

relevance_reason: A PET study of two brothers with early-onset parkinsonism caused by parkin mutations. It describes how their nigrostriatal dopaminergic function differs from sporadic PD.

findings.statement: Portman et al. (2001) used PET to measure nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and cerebral energy metabolism in 2 brothers with early-onset parkinsonism caused by mutation in the parkin gene. Cerebral energy metabolism did not differ from that in sporadic PD, but the nigrostriatal dopaminergic pattern was clearly different. The authors concluded that parkinsonism in these 2 patients was pathophysiologically different from PD.
quotes: Nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and cerebral energy metabolism were measured with PET in two brothers with early-onset parkinsonism caused by mutation of the parkin gene.
Energy metabolism did not differ, but the nigrostriatal dopaminergic pattern was clearly different than that of sporadic PD.
Thus parkinsonism in these two patients was shown to be pathophysiologically different than PD.

phenotypes.text: abnormal nigrostriatal dopaminergic pattern on PET

relevance_reason: Reports a family with autosomal recessive early-onset parkinsonism carrying compound heterozygous parkin mutations, with clinical and neuropathologic findings.

findings.statement: van de Warrenburg et al. (2001) described a Dutch family with autosomal recessive early-onset parkinsonism. Although parkinsonism was the main clinical syndrome, the proband also had mild gait ataxia.
quotes: A Dutch family with autosomal recessive early-onset parkinsonism showed a heterozygous missense mutation in combination with a heterozygous exon deletion in the parkin gene.
Although the main clinical syndrome consisted of parkinsonism, the proband clinically had additional mild gait ataxia

findings.statement: On neuropathologic examination of the proband, van de Warrenburg et al. (2001) found selective loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, along with neuronal loss in parts of the spinocerebellar system. There were no Lewy bodies or neurofibrillary tangles, but tau pathology was present.
quotes: pathologically showed neuronal loss in parts of the spinocerebellar system, in addition to selective loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta
Lewy bodies and neurofibrillary tangles were absent, but tau pathology was found.

phenotypes.text: loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta

phenotypes.hpo_label: Neuronal loss in central nervous system

findings.statement: In the Dutch family with autosomal recessive early-onset parkinsonism, van de Warrenburg et al. (2001) found compound heterozygous mutations in the parkin gene: a heterozygous missense mutation together with a heterozygous exon deletion.
quotes: A Dutch family with autosomal recessive early-onset parkinsonism showed a heterozygous missense mutation in combination with a heterozygous exon deletion in the parkin gene.

relevance_reason: An autopsy case of AR-JP with a homozygous deletion of parkin exon 4, reporting neuropathology and the genetic finding.

findings.statement: Hayashi et al. (2000) reported a 70-year-old man with autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP). At age 32 years he developed a dystonic gait. Hand tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia and impaired postural reflexes followed. Levodopa improved these symptoms.
quotes: We report the neuropathologic and genetic features of a 70-year-old man with autosomal-recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP).
At the age of 32 years, he developed a dystonic gait, followed by hand tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, and impaired postural reflex. Levodopa was effective in ameliorating these symptoms.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

findings.statement: At autopsy, Hayashi et al. (2000) found loss of pigmented neurons with gliosis in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNPC) and the locus ceruleus. In the SNPC the loss was most pronounced in the medial and ventrolateral regions. The remaining SNPC neurons had low melanin content, which was less marked in the locus ceruleus. Immunostaining for alpha-synuclein confirmed there were no Lewy bodies. The authors also found neuronal loss and fibrillary gliosis in the substantia nigra pars reticulata, which they noted had not been reported before in AR-JP.
quotes: Pathologic examination of autopsy specimens from this patient revealed loss of pigmented neurons and gliosis in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNPC), being most pronounced in the medial and ventrolateral regions, and locus ceruleus (LC).
There were no Lewy bodies, as confirmed by immunostaining for alpha-synuclein.
An additional, significant finding in this patient was neuronal loss and fibrillary gliosis in the substantia nigra pars reticulata; this feature has not been reported previously in AR-JP.

phenotypes.text: loss of pigmented neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta

phenotypes.hpo_label: Neuronal loss in central nervous system

findings.statement: Hayashi et al. (2000) found a homozygous deletion of exon 4 of the parkin gene in the autopsied patient with AR-JP and in his siblings.
quotes: Gene analysis revealed that this autopsied patient and his siblings had the parkin gene mutation (homozygous exon 4 deletion) that is responsible for the disease.

relevance_reason: Reports compound heterozygous parkin deletions in a family with adult-onset, tremor-dominant parkinsonism, which widens the PARK2 phenotype.

findings.statement: Klein et al. (2000) described a large pedigree from South Tyrol, northern Italy, with adult-onset, clinically typical tremor-dominant parkinsonism that appeared to be autosomal dominant. The 4 affected male sibs could not be clinically distinguished from most patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease. None had the hallmarks reported with earlier parkin mutations: diurnal fluctuations, benefit from sleep, foot dystonia, hyperreflexia, or early susceptibility to levodopa-induced dyskinesias.
quotes: Here we present a large pedigree from South Tyrol (a region of northern Italy) with adult-onset, clinically typical tremor-dominant parkinsonism of apparently autosomal dominant inheritance.
The patients were clinically indistinguishable from most patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease.

None of them displayed any of the clinical hallmarks described in patients with previously reported parkin mutations, including diurnal fluctuations, benefit from sleep, foot dystonia, hyperreflexia, and early susceptibility to levodopa-induced dyskinesias.

findings.statement: In this South Tyrolean family, Klein et al. (2000) used haplotype analysis to exclude linkage to the chromosome 2p, 4p and 4q regions that contain genes for autosomal dominant parkinsonism. The analysis instead implicated the parkin locus on chromosome 6q.
quotes: Haplotype analysis excluded linkage to the chromosome 2p, 4p, and 4q regions that harbor genes associated with autosomal dominant parkinsonism, but implicated the parkin locus on chromosome 6q.

findings.statement: Klein et al. (2000) found compound heterozygous deletions in the parkin gene, one large and one truncating, in the 4 affected male sibs. Two affected women in the family carried only the truncating deletion, in the heterozygous state with an apparently normal second allele.
quotes: Compound heterozygous deletions in the parkin gene (one large and one truncating) were identified in 4 affected male siblings.
Two affected female individuals carried one (truncating) of the two deletions in a heterozygous state with an apparently normal allele.

findings.statement: Klein et al. (2000) concluded that parkin mutations cause a wider range of phenotypes than previously reported. They suggested that the gene may be important in the etiology of the more common late-onset typical Parkinson disease.
quotes: We conclude that the phenotypic spectrum associated with mutations in the parkin gene is broader than previously reported, suggesting that this gene may be important in the etiology of the more frequent late-onset typical Parkinson's disease.

relevance_reason: Autopsy pathology and biochemical study of a patient with 6q-linked AR-JP (PARK2); only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Mori et al. (1998) reported pathologic and biochemical studies in a patient with 6q-linked autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP). Neuronal loss and gliosis were confined to the substantia nigra and the locus ceruleus, and no Lewy bodies were found. Neurofibrillary tangles and argyrophilic astrocytes were seen in the cerebral cortex and brainstem nuclei, which the authors said had not been reported before in AR-JP.
quotes: Neuronal loss and gliosis were restricted to the substantia nigra and the locus ceruleus.
No Lewy bodies were found, but neurofibrillary tangles and argyrophilic astrocytes were seen in the cerebral cortex and brainstem nuclei.

phenotypes.text: neuronal loss and gliosis of the substantia nigra
neuronal loss of the locus ceruleus
phenotypes.hpo_label: Neuronal loss in central nervous system

phenotypes.text: neurofibrillary tangles in cerebral cortex and brainstem nuclei

findings.statement: Mori et al. (1998) suggested that the finding of neurofibrillary tangles and argyrophilic astrocytes in their patient pointed to pathologic heterogeneity in 6q-linked AR-JP.
quotes: The later findings, which have not been reported previously in AR-JP, suggest the pathologic heterogeneity of 6q-linked AR-JP.

relevance_reason: Linkage study confirming and refining the mapping of autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism to 6q25.2-q27 in 15 families from four ethnic groups.

findings.statement: Jones et al. (1998) found linkage of autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism to 6q25.2-q27 in 15 families from four distinct ethnic backgrounds. A full genomic screen excluded other candidate regions. Using a detailed genetic map of the linked region, they found that recombination events restricted the JP locus to a 6.9-cM region.
quotes: We found linkage to this region in a group of 15 families from four distinct ethnic backgrounds. A full genomic screen excluded other candidate regions.
Recombination events restricted the JP locus to a 6.9-cM region and excluded SOD2.

findings.statement: Jones et al. (1998) mapped the manganese superoxide dismutase gene (SOD2), a candidate gene, within the linked region, and recombination events excluded SOD2 as the JP gene.
quotes: have mapped the position of the manganese superoxide dismutase gene (SOD2). Recombination events restricted the JP locus to a 6.9-cM region and excluded SOD2.

findings.statement: Jones et al. (1998) observed apparent homozygosity for null alleles at marker D6S955 in one family, which suggested a deletion and finer localization of the JP locus.
quotes: The apparent homozygosity for null alleles at D6S955 in one family suggested a deletion and finer localization of the JP locus.

relevance_reason: Linkage study confirming the PARK2 locus for AR juvenile parkinsonism in European and Algerian families. It narrows the candidate region, reports a homozygous deletion of microsatellite markers and widens the clinical spectrum.

findings.statement: Tassin et al. (1998) tested 1 Algerian and 10 European multiplex families with early-onset Parkinson disease for linkage to the AR-JP locus on chromosome 6q25.2-q27 using marker D6S305. Homogeneity analysis gave a conditional probability in favor of linkage of greater than 0.9 in 8 families. These 8 families were analyzed further with 8 microsatellite markers spanning the 17-cM region. Haplotype reconstruction and the smallest region of homozygosity in 2 consanguineous families reduced the candidate interval to 11.3 cM.
quotes: We have tested one Algerian and 10 European multiplex families with early-onset Parkinson disease for linkage to this locus, with marker D6S305.
Homogeneity analysis provided a conditional probability in favor of linkage of >.9 in eight families
Haplotype reconstruction for eight families and determination of the smallest region of homozygosity in two consanguineous families reduced the candidate interval to 11.3 cM.

findings.statement: In the Algerian family, Tassin et al. (1998) found a deletion of 2 microsatellite markers, D6S411 and D6S1550, which colocalize on the genetic map and segregated with the disease. The title describes this as a small homozygous deletion. The authors noted that if this deletion is taken into account, the candidate region would be reduced to less than 1 cM.
quotes: If the deletion of two microsatellite markers (D6S411 and D6S1550) that colocalize on the genetic map and that segregate with the disease in the Algerian family is taken into account, the candidate region would be reduced to <1 cM.
evidence of a small homozygous deletion in one family

findings.statement: Tassin et al. (1998) confirmed linkage of AR-JP to the PARK2 locus in European families and in an Algerian family. They concluded that PARK2 appears to be an important locus for AR-JP in European patients. Linkage was favored in 8 of the 11 families tested.
quotes: We have confirmed linkage of AR-JP, in European families and in an Algerian family, to the PARK2 locus. PARK2 appears to be an important locus for AR-JP in European patients.

findings.statement: Tassin et al. (1998) found that the clinical spectrum of chromosome 6-linked AR early-onset parkinsonism in their families was broader than previously reported. Age at onset was up to 58 years, and some patients had painful dystonia.
quotes: The clinical spectrum of the disease in our families, with age at onset <=58 years and the presence of painful dystonia in some patients, is broader than that reported previously.

relevance_reason: Refines the linkage mapping of the AR-JP (PARK2) locus on 6q25.2-27 and identifies markers in linkage disequilibrium.

findings.statement: Saito et al. (1998) narrowed the AR-JP locus on chromosome 6q25.2-27 by linkage analysis with densely spaced markers. The highest cumulative pairwise lod score was 9.13 at D6S1579 (theta = 0.05), and the highest cumulative multipoint lod score was 12.4 at a locus 3 cM telomeric to D6S1599. Obligate recombination events reduced the candidate region to 13 cM between D6S1579 and D6S264.
quotes: Pairwise linkage analysis revealed the highest cumulative maximal lod score of 9.13 at D6S1579 (theta = 0.05), and multipoint linkage analysis revealed the highest cumulative lod score of 12.4 at the locus 3 cM telomeric to D6S1599.
Observation of obligate recombination events narrowed the candidate region to a 13-cM region between D6S1579 and D6S264.

findings.statement: Saito et al. (1998) found strong linkage disequilibrium between the AR-JP locus and 2 markers: D6S1579 (chi-square 84.22, P < 0.0001; lambda = 0.40) and D6S1599 (chi-square 63.37, P < 0.0001; lambda = 0.30). They suggested that the AR-JP gene most likely lies near the 4-cM region containing these 2 markers.
quotes: we identified two marker loci, D6S1579 and D6S1599, which exhibit strong linkage disequilibrium with the AR-JP locus
These results suggest that the candidate region for the AR-JP gene is most likely located near the 4-cM region encompassing D6S1579 and D6S1599.

findings.statement: Saito et al. (1998) described autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism as a hereditary neurodegenerative disorder with parkinsonism that responds to levodopa. Mean age at onset was 23.2 years.
quotes: Autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP) (MIM 600116) is a hereditary neurodegenerative disorder characterized by levodopa-responsive parkinsonism with a mean age at onset of 23.2 years.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

relevance_reason: Maps early-onset parkinsonism with diurnal fluctuation to the ARJP/PARK2 locus on 6q and concludes the two are allelic, which defines the alternative title of this entry.

findings.statement: Matsumine et al. (1998) described early-onset parkinsonism with diurnal fluctuation (EPDF) as a dopa-responsive parkinsonism with early onset in which parkinsonian symptoms improved after sleep. In a pathologic study of one EPDF case, they found selective neuronal degeneration in the zona compacta of the substantia nigra without Lewy body formation.
quotes: Early onset parkinsonism with diurnal fluctuation (EPDF) is a dopa-responsive parkinsonism characterized by early onset and improvement of parkinsonian symptoms after sleep.
A pathologic study of one case of EPDF showed selective neuronal degeneration in the zona compacta of the substantia nigra without Lewy body formation.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

phenotypes.text: improvement of symptoms after sleep (diurnal fluctuation)
selective neuronal degeneration of substantia nigra zona compacta

findings.statement: Matsumine et al. (1998) studied 53 members of 17 EPDF families (151 meioses). Multipoint linkage analysis gave a peak lod score of 14.2 at 1.0 cM telomeric to D6S305 and placed the disease locus in a 17-cM interval between D6S437 and D6S253, the same position mapped for autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (ARJP). The highest two-point lod score was 10.13 at theta = 0 for D6S305, and haplotype analysis agreed with the multipoint result.
quotes: the authors examined 53 members of 17 EPDF families and analyzed 151 meioses.

Multipoint linkage analysis gave a peak lod score of 14.2 at 1.0 cM telomeric to D6S305 and placed the disease locus in the 17-cM interval between D6S437 and D6S253, which is exactly the same position mapped for autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism
The highest two-point lod score was obtained at D6S305 (10.13 at theta = 0). Haplotype analysis agreed with the result of multipoint analysis.

findings.statement: Matsumine et al. (1998) found that 8 of the 17 EPDF families were nonconsanguineous, that the families shared no common haplotypes, and that the families came from widely separated geographic origins. They suggested that EPDF has multiple founder mutations.
quotes: A high proportion of nonconsanguinity (8/17 families), the absence of commonly shared haplotypes, and the widespread geographic distribution of the families' origins suggest that EPDF has multiple founder mutations.

findings.statement: Matsumine et al. (1998) concluded that EPDF and ARJP are allelic disorders and should be included in the spectrum of a single clinicogenetic entity, chromosome 6q-linked parkinsonism. They described this disease as having a benign clinical course and relatively selective degeneration of nigral dopaminergic neurons without Lewy body formation.
quotes: The authors concluded that EPDF and ARJP are allelic disorders and should be included in the spectrum of a single-clinicogenetic entity of chromosome 6q-linked parkinsonism.
This disease could be characterized by a benign clinical course and relatively selective degeneration of nigral dopaminergic neurons with no Lewy body formation.

relevance_reason: This paper reports the positional cloning of the parkin gene and deletions in it in patients with autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism, which establishes the gene behind PARK2.

findings.statement: Kitada et al. (1998) noted that AR-JP had been mapped to 6q25.2-q27 and was strongly linked to markers D6S305 and D6S253, and that D6S305 was deleted in 1 Japanese AR-JP patient. They used positional cloning within this microdeletion to isolate the causative gene.
quotes: Autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP) maps to the long arm of chromosome 6 (6q25.2-q27) and is linked strongly to the markers D6S305 and D6S253; the former is deleted in one Japanese AR-JP patient.

findings.statement: Kitada et al. (1998) isolated a 2,960-bp cDNA with a 1,395-bp open reading frame. It encoded a 465-amino acid protein with moderate similarity to ubiquitin at the N terminus and a RING-finger motif at the C terminus. They named the protein 'Parkin'. A 4.5-kb transcript was expressed in many human tissues and was abundant in brain, including the substantia nigra.
