quotes: we have now isolated a complementary DNA done of 2,960 base pairs with a 1,395-base-pair open reading frame, encoding a protein of 465 amino acids with moderate similarity to ubiquitin at the amino terminus and a RING-finger motif at the carboxy terminus
A 4.5-kilobase transcript that is expressed in many human tissues but is abundant in the brain, including the substantia nigra

findings.statement: Kitada et al. (1998) found that the parkin gene spans more than 500 kb and contains 12 exons.
quotes: The gene spans more than 500 kilobases and has 12 exons

findings.statement: Kitada et al. (1998) found a deletion of exons 3 through 7 of the parkin gene in a Japanese AR-JP patient who carried a microdeletion at D6S305.
quotes: five of which (exons 3-7) are deleted in the patient

findings.statement: Kitada et al. (1998) found a deletion affecting only exon 4 of the parkin gene in 4 AR-JP patients from 3 unrelated families. In brain tissue from 1 group of exon-4-deleted patients, the 4.5-kb parkin transcript was shorter. The authors concluded that mutations in parkin appear to be responsible for AR-JP.
quotes: Four other AR-JP patients from three unrelated families have a deletion affecting exon 4 alone.
is shorter in brain tissue from one of the groups of exon-4-deleted patients
Mutations in the newly identified gene appear to be responsible for the pathogenesis of AR-JP

relevance_reason: Original linkage mapping of the AR-JP (PARK2) locus to chromosome 6q25.2-27.

findings.statement: Matsumine et al. (1997) found a family with autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP) in which the disease segregated perfectly with a diallelic polymorphism of the Mn-superoxide dismutase gene (SOD2). Extending linkage analysis to 13 families with AR-JP, they mapped the AR-JP gene to chromosome 6q25.2-27, including the SOD2 locus, with maximum cumulative pairwise lod scores of 7.26 at D6S305 (theta = 0.03) and 7.71 at D6S253 (theta = 0.02). Obligate recombination events and multipoint linkage analysis placed the gene in a 17-cM interval between D6S437 and D6S264.
quotes: By linkage analysis of diallelic polymorphism of the Mn-superoxide dismutase gene (SOD2), we found a family with AR-JP showing perfect segregation of the disease with the SOD2 locus.

By extending the linkage analysis to 13 families with AR-JP, we discovered strong evidence for the localization of the AR-JP gene at chromosome 6q25.2-27, including the SOD2 locus, with the maximal cumulative pairwise LOD scores of 7.26 and 7.71 at D6S305 (theta = .03) and D6S253 (theta = .02), respectively.
Observation of obligate recombination events, as well as multipoint linkage analysis, placed the AR-JP gene in a 17-cM interval between D6S437 and D6S264.

findings.statement: Matsumine et al. (1997) described autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism as a levodopa-responsive parkinsonism whose pathologic finding is a highly selective degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the zona compacta of the substantia nigra.
quotes: An autosomal recessive form of juvenile Parkinsonism (AR-JP) (MIM 600116) is a levodopa-responsive Parkinsonism whose pathological finding is a highly selective degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the zona compacta of the substantia nigra.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

phenotypes.text: selective degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta

relevance_reason: Clinical characterization of 17 Japanese patients with autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP), defining the PARK2 phenotype.

findings.statement: Ishikawa and Tsuji (1996) described the clinical features of 17 patients from 12 Japanese families with autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP). There was female predominance, mean age at onset was 27.8 years, and progression was slow. The parkinsonian triad of tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia was mild, whereas gait freezing, hyperreflexia, foot dystonia, and retropulsion were relatively prominent.
quotes: Analysis of the clinical features showed female predominance, mean age at onset 27.8 years, and slow progression.
The symptoms of the parkinsonian triad (tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia) were mild, but gait freezing, hyperreflexia, foot dystonia, and retropulsion were relatively prominent.

findings.statement: Ishikawa and Tsuji (1996) found that all 17 patients with AR-JP had amelioration of parkinsonian symptoms after sleep, which they considered a characteristic finding.
quotes: A characteristic finding was amelioration of parkinsonian symptoms after sleep in all patients.

phenotypes.text: improvement of parkinsonian symptoms after sleep

findings.statement: Ishikawa and Tsuji (1996) reported that response to levodopa in AR-JP patients was satisfactory, but levodopa-induced choreic limb dyskinesia and the wearing-off phenomenon occurred frequently.
quotes: Response to levodopa was satisfactory, but dopa-induced choreic limb dyskinesia and wearing-off phenomenon occurred frequently.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

findings.statement: Ishikawa and Tsuji (1996) strongly suspected autosomal recessive inheritance of juvenile parkinsonism in their 12 Japanese families because the parents were consanguineous in all but 1 family and all patients were in a single generation.
quotes: Because the marriages of the parents in all but one family were consanguineous and all patients were only first generation, an autosomal-recessive trait was strongly suspected.

findings.statement: Ishikawa and Tsuji (1996) concluded that AR-JP is a distinct clinical entity within juvenile parkinsonism. They based this on the similar clinical findings among their patients and the differences from other types of parkinsonism.
quotes: The similarity of clinical findings in these patients, and the differences from other types of parkinsonism, indicates that AR-JP is distinct clinical entity.

relevance_reason: Clinical and pathologic description of a consanguineous family with juvenile-onset parkinsonism that improves after sleep, the phenotype defining this entry.

findings.statement: Takahashi et al. (1994) described a family in which 4 of 5 sibs developed parkinsonism with similar onset at an early age. The parkinsonism improved following sleep. The parents were first cousins.
quotes: We describe a family with juvenile-onset parkinsonism, which improved following sleep.
Four of the five siblings in this family developed a similar onset of parkinsonism at an early age, and the parents were first cousins.

findings.statement: Takahashi et al. (1994) reported affected sibs born to first-cousin parents in a family with juvenile parkinsonism.
quotes: Four of the five siblings in this family developed a similar onset of parkinsonism at an early age, and the parents were first cousins.

findings.statement: Takahashi et al. (1994) reported the autopsy of one affected sib, a 67-year-old woman. Pathologic changes were confined to the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNPC) and the locus ceruleus. The medial and ventrolateral SNPC showed obvious neuronal loss and gliosis. Elsewhere in the SNPC and in the locus ceruleus, neurons were fewer and most had low melanin content, with no detectable gliosis or extraneuronal free melanin. There were no Lewy bodies, and the authors concluded that the overall pathology differed from that of Lewy body Parkinson disease.
quotes: In one of the siblings, a 67-year-old woman, pathologic changes at autopsy were confined to the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNPC) and locus ceruleus. The SNPC revealed obvious neuronal loss and gliosis in the medial and ventrolateral regions.
There were no Lewy bodies. The entire pathologic picture was different from that of Lewy body Parkinson's disease.

the population of neurons was reduced and there was low melanin content in most of the neurons but no detectable gliosis or extraneuronal free melanin pigment suggestive of a neurodegenerative process.

phenotypes.text: neuronal loss and gliosis in substantia nigra pars compacta

phenotypes.hpo_label: Neuronal loss in central nervous system

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It reports anticipation of onset age in familial Parkinson disease in general, not specifically autosomal recessive juvenile PARK2, so it gives context only.

findings.statement: Bonifati et al. (1994) reported anticipation of onset age in familial Parkinson disease.
quotes: Anticipation of onset age in familial Parkinson's disease.

relevance_reason: The paper describes two siblings with hereditary early-onset parkinsonism that responded to anticholinergics but not levodopa. The authors propose it as a variant distinct from the levodopa-sensitive juvenile forms, which makes it useful for heterogeneity and differential context in the juvenile AR PD entry. No gene or variant is reported.

findings.statement: Mitsui et al. (1994) reported 2 sibs with hereditary parkinsonism accompanied by pyramidal signs and cerebellar ataxia. Anticholinergic drugs had a dramatic beneficial effect in both sibs, but levodopa did not. The authors proposed this as a new hereditary variant of early-onset Parkinson disease, distinct from the levodopa-sensitive forms of juvenile Parkinson disease.
quotes: Two siblings who exhibited hereditary parkinsonism with pyramidal signs and cerebellar ataxia are reported.
Anticholinergics had a dramatic beneficial effect in both cases, but levodopa did not.
We propose a new hereditary variant of early onset Parkinson's disease distinct from the levodopa sensitive forms of juvenile Parkinson's disease.

findings.statement: Mitsui et al. (1994) noted that the response to anticholinergics in their sibs resembled the response reported in patients with Joseph disease. They suggested that it pointed to dysfunction of an 'indirect pathway' involving the globus pallidus and the subthalamic nucleus, in addition to dysfunction of the nigrostriatal system.
quotes: This responsiveness, which is similar to that reported in patients with Joseph's disease, suggests dysfunction of an "indirect pathway" involving the globus pallidus and the subthalamic nucleus, in addition to that of the nigrostriatal system.

relevance_reason: The abstract describes a family with autosomal dominant hereditary juvenile dystonia-parkinsonism. The features resemble PARK2 (sleep benefit, response to levodopa, wearing-off, levodopa-induced dyskinesia), but the inheritance is dominant rather than recessive and no gene or mapping data are given. It is useful only as context or as possible evidence of heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Ishikawa and Miyatake (1995) reported a family with hereditary juvenile dystonia-parkinsonism in which 8 members in 3 generations were affected, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance. The authors considered the patients to have a specific form of hereditary dystonia-parkinsonism.
quotes: We report a family with autosomal dominant type hereditary juvenile dystonia-parkinsonism in which eight members in three generations exhibited parkinsonism
From the family history and clinical findings, these patients are considered to have a specific form of hereditary dystonia-parkinsonism.

findings.statement: Ishikawa and Miyatake (1995) described 8 affected members of 1 family with juvenile dystonia-parkinsonism. They had parkinsonism, sleep benefit, a marked response to levodopa, wearing-off phenomenon and levodopa-induced choreic dyskinesia. The patients also had neck dystonia (torticollis and retrocollis), foot dystonia and other dystonic movements, such as frequently lifting the thigh. In 1 patient the main feature was dystonic movement, which worsened after levodopa was given.
quotes: eight members in three generations exhibited parkinsonism, sleep benefit, marked efficacy of levodopa, wearing-off phenomenon, and dopa-induced choreic dyskinesia
However, one case showed mainly dystonic movement that worsened after administration of levodopa.
The patients in this family showed neck dystonia, such as torticollis and retrocollis, in addition to foot dystonia and other dystonic movement, such as frequently lifting the thigh.

Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

relevance_reason: The title describes early-onset paralysis agitans (parkinsonism) with marked diurnal fluctuation of symptoms, which matches this entry's alternative title. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Yamamura et al. (1973) described paralysis agitans (parkinsonism) with early onset and marked diurnal fluctuation of symptoms.
quotes: Paralysis agitans of early onset with marked diurnal fluctuation of symptoms.
